A-I1.quote: This review presents an all-inclusive assessment of recent advancements in spatio-temporal CI estimation using smart meter data, BTM based SPV disaggregation, machine learning (ML) based analytics and cybersecurity frameworks within in smart grids.

A-I2.quote: Smart meter data constitutes the primary dataset, which provides high-frequency elec­ tricity consumption measurement at the consumer level.

A-I3.quote: Moreover, cybersecurity threats, mainly false data injection attacks (FDIAs) are discussed along with privacy preserving approaches viz., anomaly detection and encrypted mechanisms.

A-I4.quote: Next Energy 13 (2026) 100953 Contents lists available at ScienceDirect

A-I5.quote: Received 9 May 2026; Received in revised form 30 July 2026; Accepted 23 August 2026

parsed.rationale: This is a peer-reviewed 2026 review article in Next Energy. Its main contribution is a synthesis of work on carbon-intensity estimation from smart-meter and BTM data, and it treats the 'unified framework' as an organising structure for that synthesis. Privacy is not a stated aim and has no dedicated section or comparison column: Table 7's dimensions are CI, BTM, DER, ML and cyber concerns. Privacy appears only as one row in Tables 6 and 11 ('may reveal their behaviour'), as passing mentions of federated learning and encryption, and in a short remark in 'What's next', so A-I3 is not met (A-E6).

A-I2.quote: Despite their advantages, SGs raise significant privacy concerns due to the fine-grained energy data collected by SMs [14].

parsed.rationale: This is a peer-reviewed Elsevier journal survey (2025). Its main contribution is a synthesis of privacy-preserving schemes for smart grids and smart-meter data published 2018–2024, and its own taxonomy and recommendations are minor synthesis elements. Privacy is the stated main theme in the title and abstract. The paper also covers privacy attacks and inference risks, such as consumption data revealing routines and occupancy (Sections 1.1 and 3.3.3), so it is not mechanism-only.

A-I1.quote: With this systematic mapping study, we will provide an overview of the current literature and attempt to determine the future directions the research may take.

A-I2.quote: In this mapping study, we analyzed 55 papers on differential privacy applied to the smart grid

A-I3.quote: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) attacks use the electricity usage of a household over time to try and determine what appliances are being used, and from that learn the occupancy and schedules of the household.

A-I4.quote: In The 36th ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC ’21), March 22–26, 2021, Virtual Event, Republic of Korea. ACM, New York, NY, USA

A-I5.quote: SAC ’21, March 22–26, 2021, Virtual Event, Republic of Korea © 2021 Association for Computing Machinery.

parsed.rationale: The paper is a systematic mapping study of 55 papers on differential privacy applied to smart meters and the smart grid, published at ACM SAC 2021. Privacy is its main theme, as shown in the title and abstract. It is a DP-mechanism survey, but it goes beyond a motivating mention of risks: Section 4.2 has a paragraph explaining how linkage, differencing and NILM-based inference attacks work. The background section also lists inferable household details such as economic status and occupancy, so the mechanism_only flag does not apply.

A-I1.quote: We provide a review of existing works highlighting the importance of energy consumption as valuable personal data as well as an analysis of the established Smart Grid Architecture Model and its main challenges from a legal viewpoint

A-I2.quote: The Smart Grid has similar features as any privacy-critical system but, in comparison to the engineering of other architectures, has the peculiarity of being the source of energy consumption data.

A-I3.quote: Electricity consumption constitutes an indirect means to infer personal information. This work looks at the Smart Grid from the perspective of the GDPR

A-I4.quote: © The Author(s) 2020 A. Siarheyeva et al. (Eds.): ISD 2019, LNISO 39, pp. 113–130, 2020.

A-I5.quote: © The Author(s) 2020 A. Siarheyeva et al. (Eds.): ISD 2019, LNISO 39, pp. 113–130, 2020.

parsed.rationale: The abstract names two contributions: a review of existing works and the authors' own legal analysis of the Smart Grid Architecture Model. That analysis is developed in its own sections: Sect. 3 maps identifiers and consumption data through the SGAM layers, and Sect. 4 classifies GDPR challenges. The own legal/conceptual analysis is therefore a main contribution and A-I1 is not met, so the code is A-E1 with route none (it is neither an attack nor a privacy-preserving mechanism). Domain, privacy focus, venue (Springer LNISO, ISD 2019 conference) and year are all satisfied.

A-I2.quote: Smart Grid Metering Networks: A Survey on Security, Privacy and Open Research Issues

parsed.rationale: This is a survey published in IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials in 2019, and its main contribution is a review of existing threats and countermeasures for smart metering networks. Privacy is part of the title and the stated aims. It also has dedicated sections: Section VII on threats to privacy, including inference of daily routine from consumption data, and Section X on privacy countermeasures. The threat taxonomy and the list of requirements are the authors' own, but they are synthesis devices rather than a primary contribution.
